system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's zero-shot (leave-one-modality-out) training, the segmentation adapters — the only part that produces anomaly maps — are trained with Dice and Focal losses exclusively on the three source datasets that have pixel masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC), while OCT17, ChestXray and HIS only train the detection adapters. Primary question: can the segmentation adapters be trained from image-level labels alone, and how much mask-supervised localisation does that retain on the unseen modality? At each of the four adapter levels, with the original level weights, the Dice and Focal terms are replaced by an image-level BCE on the top-k mean of the level's patch-to-text anomaly probabilities (k = 1% of patches), applied to all five source datasets with every mask discarded; the detection adapters and their loss are unchanged. Hypothesis: because patch scores are similarities to text anchors shared by all modalities, this weak supervision yields localisation that transfers to the unseen modality. Primary outcomes: pixel-level AUROC and AUPRO on the held-out folds with masks (BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC) and image-level AUROC on all folds, mask-supervised versus image-label-supervised MVFA under the shared protocol. Secondary analyses: (i) a control in which the text anchors of the segmentation branch are replaced by a learned linear patch classifier trained with the same MIL loss, isolating the role of the text anchors; (ii) a per-level breakdown; (iii) two label-budget points with masks for 10% and 25% of the abnormal source images (one seed, two folds).

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Asymmetric sigmoid MIL for mask-free MVFA segmentation adapters
SUMMARY: Train MVFA's segmentation adapters from image labels only: every patch of a normal image is pushed to the normal anchor and the top-1% patches of an abnormal image to the abnormal anchor, with a SigLIP-style sigmoid loss at all four levels.
HYPOTHESIS: Asymmetric sigmoid MIL on image labels from all five source datasets retains at least 75% of mask-supervised MVFA's pixel-AUROC margin over chance on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT and RESC, and exceeds the symmetric top-k BCE MIL of the problem statement by at least 2 pixel-AUROC points.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: segmentation supervision (Dice+Focal on masks; symmetric top-k BCE MIL as in the problem; asymmetric sigmoid MIL). For level l and patch j, z_j = t (cos(f_j, T_abn) - cos(f_j, T_nor)) + b with learnable t, b. Normal image: mean over all patches of softplus(z_j). Abnormal image: mean over the top-k patches (k = 1% of patches, at least 3) of softplus(-z_j), plus 0.1 x mean over the bottom 50% of softplus(z_j) (most of an abnormal image is normal tissue). Dependent variables: pixel AUROC, AUPRO, image AUROC on the held-out modality, and retention = (AUROC_MIL - 0.5)/(AUROC_mask - 0.5).
RATIONALE: A normal image carries a pixel-level label for free: every patch is normal. Only abnormal images are ambiguous. The problem's symmetric top-k MIL wastes this: a normal image constrains only its k most anomalous patches. An asymmetric objective supervises all patches of normal images and only the most anomalous patches of abnormal images, with MadCLIP's sigmoid patch-text loss, which tolerates the many-to-one patch/anchor relation.
METHOD: 1) loss.py: add asym_mil_loss(seg_patch_tokens, text_features, label, t, b, k_frac=0.01) computing per-level cosines (tokens L2-normalised as in MVFA), the normal-all-patches term and the abnormal top-k term with the bottom-50% term; sum over the four levels with MVFA's level weights. 2) train_zero.py: replace the seg branch's Focal+Dice block (executed only when the dataset has masks) by asym_mil_loss for every image; t (init 10) and b (init -5) are nn.Parameters in the seg optimizer; detection branch unchanged. 3) Hyper-parameters: Adam, lr and epochs as in the released script, batch size 1 as in the code; k_frac in {0.5%, 1%, 2%}; bottom-term weight 0.1. 4) Inference unchanged (test_zero.py).
EXPERIMENT: Protocol: BMAD zero-shot, leave-one-modality-out (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded for the image-label variants; checkpoints selected on a validation split of the source modalities by image AUROC (no masks used for selection); mask-supervised MVFA re-run under the same rule as the reference; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds; a one-fold pilot monitors the fraction of normal-image patches above 0.5 to detect collapsed maps. Baselines: mask-supervised MVFA; symmetric top-k BCE MIL (the problem's operator). Ablations: k_frac; bottom-50% term on/off; sigmoid vs. BCE-on-probabilities; which levels receive the loss. Falsified if retention is below 60% or there is no gain over symmetric MIL.

Idea B:
TITLE: Witness-rate-adaptive MIL: estimating each dataset's lesion fraction by positive-unlabelled mixture-proportion estimation
SUMMARY: Replace the fixed k = 1% of the MIL operator by a per-dataset witness rate estimated from image labels alone — the fraction of patches in abnormal images whose scores are not explained by the normal-image score distribution — and update it during training.
HYPOTHESIS: Per-dataset witness-rate-adaptive k improves held-out pixel AUROC by at least 1.5 points over the best single fixed k chosen on source validation, and the estimated witness rates rank the three masked source datasets in the same order as their true median lesion areas.
RATIONALE: The asymmetric-MIL parent and the problem both fix k, yet BMAD's lesions range from small retinal fluid pockets to large brain tumours and diffuse chest findings, so any single k is wrong for most datasets. Positive-unlabelled learning offers an analogous principle: patches of abnormal images are an unlabelled mixture of normal and lesion patches, and patches of normal images are a clean sample of the normal component. The mixture proportion (the witness rate) can be estimated from the two score distributions (for example by the best-bin estimator of Scott, 2015) and used as k for that dataset. No masks are needed, and the estimate is checkable against the masks that do exist.
METHOD: 1) loss.py: topk_mil with per-dataset k_d. 2) train_zero.py: every 2 epochs, on a held-out portion of each source dataset, collect level-4 patch probabilities of normal and abnormal images; estimate pi_d = min over thresholds t of (1 - F_abn(t))/(1 - F_norm(t)) (best-bin estimator, upper-bounded by 0.5); set k_d = max(3 patches, pi_d x number of patches); first 2 epochs use k = 1%. 3) Hyper-parameters: update interval 2 epochs; clipping [0.5%, 30%]. Inference unchanged.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out zero-shot training on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together); all source masks discarded; checkpoints selected on source-modality validation by image AUROC; mask-supervised MVFA and the problem's plain top-k MIL re-run under the same rule; 3 seeds, mean and std; pixel AUROC and AUPRO on held-out BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC, image AUROC on all folds. Baselines: fixed k in {0.5%, 1%, 5%} chosen on source validation; asymmetric sigmoid MIL. Diagnostic: estimated pi_d vs. true mask area fraction on BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC. Falsified if adaptive k does not beat the best fixed k.
